sections.html:
Belleville is the St. Clair County seat in the Metro East, and its housing stock reflects almost two centuries of building. The first homes were simple brick cottages that locals called German street houses or row houses, and later decades added Foursquare, Italianate, Queen Anne and Victorian styles. A seller with a pre-war house here is often selling a property that has had many owners, many repairs and several rounds of wiring and plumbing updates.

Belleville has three locally designated historic districts: Old Belleville (1974), Hexenbuckel (1991) and Oakland (1995). A separate National Register district, listed in 1976, has 73 contributing properties. If your house sits inside one of them, ask the city's building staff what rules apply to exterior work before you sign a repair-heavy contract with a buyer.

The 2025 estimate for Belleville is 40,237 people, a 5.0 percent decline from the 42,358 in the 2020 base. With fewer people competing for the same stock, conventional buyers can take longer, so pricing matters.

Values near $141,300 and rents near $1,019 put a premium on condition. The next two sections cover the city rules that can hold up a closing for owner-occupants and landlords alike.

sections.h2: Inspection and occupancy permit when a house sells
sections.html:
Belleville requires a Residential Certificate of Occupancy before a residence can be legally occupied, and the city's Health, Housing and Building Department issues it after an inspection of the dwelling. Sellers should call for a housing inspection as soon as they decide to sell, because a passed inspection can shorten the closing timeline and help the new owner get the occupancy permit.

  • The inspection covers electrical and plumbing systems, exterior and interior structure and other readily visible areas, checked against the city's housing code.
  • Defects must be corrected before occupancy is allowed, and a failed inspection means no permit until the violations are cleared and a reinspection is done.
  • All sewer bills for the property must be paid and current before an inspection can be scheduled or a permit issued.
  • The permit for a new occupant carries a $55 fee, and rental inspections cost $65 per dwelling unit.
  • The number of people allowed in a unit depends on bedroom square footage, so check the allowed count before finalizing a sales contract.

The department is at 2300 West Main Street, Building M, Suite M113, and takes calls at 618-233-6817 (option 1 for inspections). The counter is open weekdays from 8 in the morning to 5 in the evening. Those fee figures date from a June 2022 revision, so ask the department for current amounts. Any new occupant still needs the permit after a renovation, which is worth raising when you compare offers.

Belleville has run a Crime Free Housing program since November 1, 2013, and any owner who leases a unit must register it. Registration costs $30 per dwelling unit, with renewals due by October 31 each year and fees doubling when a renewal is late.

Owners and managers must also complete the Crime Free Housing class, which the city now offers online, then email the department for a certificate. A leased unit needs a passed inspection, a nationwide background check on the tenant, the crime-free lease addendum and a signed lease before the tenant can obtain an occupancy permit. With a tenant in place, gather the registration receipt, the last passed inspection report and the lease so a buyer's lender or inspector can see the paperwork is in order.

A second failed reinspection carries a $50 fee. Vacant, tired rentals that would need work to pass are a common reason owners look at an as-is sale instead of fixing everything first.

Buyers ask about commutes and schools first, so have the facts ready.

  • High schools: Belleville Township High School District 201 runs Belleville East and Belleville West. Althoff Catholic High School is the Diocese of Belleville option, and parts of the city fall in East St. Louis District 189, Mascoutah District 19 and Freeburg District 77.
  • Grade schools: Districts 118, 119 (Belle Valley), 175 (Harmony Emge), 181 (Signal Hill), 115 (Whiteside) and 70 (Freeburg) all serve parts of Belleville, so the district depends on the street.
  • Transit and roads: Three St. Louis MetroLink stations sit in the city (Memorial Hospital, Belleville and College), and Illinois routes 15, 158, 159, 177, 13 and 161 pass through. Interstates 64 and 255 are adjacent.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in St. Clair County
sections.html:
Belleville deeds are filed at the St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds, whose office is at the county building on Public Square. The fee table for deeds received after July 1, 2023 lists $55.00 with the Rental Housing Support Program fee and $36.00 without it, with transfer tax added when applicable. The office takes cash, check or money order payable to Recorder of Deeds. Mail goes to PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222, and overnight carriers use 10 Public Square, 5th Floor.

Buyer and seller also complete the state's PTAX-203 transfer declaration, which goes to the county office. Counties may levy a 25-cent-per-$500 transfer tax and home rule municipalities may add another, so ask your closing agent which charges attach to a Belleville address. The Illinois Department of Revenue's Tax Rate Database has the rates.

Sellers who hold title through an estate or a family transfer should confirm the deed type with the title company before the closing date, since an exempt transfer is recorded differently from a sale.

sections.h2: How to appeal your assessment and pay taxes
sections.html:
Property in St. Clair County is reassessed every four years, and any change must be published in a county newspaper and mailed to the owner. If you think your value is out of line with neighbors, the first step is an informal review with the County Assessor's office. Most cases end there, but you can also file an appeal for a hearing before the Board of Review. Bring an exterior photo of your house and photos of at least three similar nearby properties, property record cards, or a recent appraisal, contract, settlement statement or deed. Evidence must reach the Board at least five days before the hearing or the assessment stands unchanged.

The Treasurer sends bills to the owner even when a lender escrows the taxes, and the owner stays responsible for penalties and interest. Unpaid taxes can lead the county to sell a lien. A principal dwelling with no more than six units can be redeemed for two and one-half years, and other property for two years. The Treasurer also runs a monthly payment plan for homeowners with the Homeowner Occupied Exemption, and online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience charge. Before closing, get this year's installment dates and a payoff figure from the Treasurer's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Belleville house with failed occupancy inspection items?
faqs.a: Yes, but the new occupant cannot get a Residential Occupancy Permit until the violations are corrected and the unit passes reinspection. Ask the Health, Housing and Building Department for the written inspection report, then decide whether to repair, credit the buyer or sell to someone who plans the work.

faqs.q: Who records the deed after a Belleville sale?
faqs.a: The St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds files it, at $55.00 with the Rental Housing Support Program fee or $36.00 without, plus transfer tax when it applies. Your title company or attorney normally handles the filing.

faqs.q: Do Belleville landlords have to register rentals before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, while the unit is leased. Each leased dwelling unit must be registered and updated by October 31 every year. Keep the registration, inspection report and lease together so the buyer can see the unit was compliant.

faqs.q: What if my Belleville assessment looks too high?
faqs.a: Start with an informal review at the County Assessor's office, then file with the Board of Review if needed. Submit comparables or an appraisal at least five days before your hearing, because late evidence leaves the assessment unchanged.

faqs.q: Does the falling population affect my Belleville sale price?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate of 40,237 is 5.0 percent under the 2020 base of 42,358. At a typical value near $141,300, condition and price both matter, so get two or three offers or a local agent's opinion before choosing a route.
